system_description.narrative_title: A Fragmenting Global Order under Energy, Finance and Tech Strain
system_description.narrative_summary: The system is one of cascading, interacting shocks: a Middle East security spiral is driving energy and maritime disruptions while a parallel Russia–Ukraine war sustains military and supply pressures. Those real-world shocks combine with rising global bond yields and hawkish central banks to tighten financing, even as great‑power economic and technology competition (trade measures, sanctions, chip/AI rivalry) fragments supply chains and alliances. Domestic politics and populist shifts in major democracies amplify policy volatility, making the order more brittle and adaptive responses harder to coordinate.
system_description.scope: Nation-states, alliances and rivalries; global energy and maritime trade flows; international financial and capital markets; strategic industries (semiconductors, AI, defense); multinational corporations; sanctions and trade policies; critical infrastructure and non-state actors that affect geopolitics and markets.
system_description.super_system: The planetary socio-economic-ecological-technological system (global civilization embedded in Earth-system constraints).
adjacent_subsystems: Global energy and maritime-trade subsystem (oil, LNG, shipping lanes, chokepoints)
International financial and monetary subsystem (bond markets, FX, central banks, cross-border capital flows)
Technological-industrial and supply-chain subsystem (semiconductors, AI infrastructure, data centers, critical minerals)

variables.name: Iran–Houthi maritime escalation
variables.description: An expanding confrontation involving Iran, its Houthi proxies, Gulf states and the United States that is shifting from episodic strikes to sustained attacks on shipping and regional infrastructure, raising risks of wider regional escalation and disruptions to maritime security.

variables.name: Russia–Ukraine war
variables.description: The large‑scale war between Russia and Ukraine, with NATO and EU states increasing arms, logistics and financial support while battlefield dynamics and intermittent diplomacy continue to reshape the fighting and European defence burdens.

variables.name: U.S.–China tech and supply‑chain rivalry
variables.description: A strategic competition led by the United States and China focused on semiconductors, AI, batteries and critical‑industry supply chains, in which export controls, court cases and industrial policy are driving partial decoupling and governance battles over advanced technology.

variables.name: North Korea military and nuclear build‑up
variables.description: Pyongyang's acceleration of nuclear and naval capabilities, accompanied by deeper ties with Russia and China, is shifting the security calculus on the Korean peninsula and raising the danger of new proliferation and regional arms competition.

variables.name: Global financial market stress and repricing
variables.description: A synchronized repricing across bond and risk markets—driven by higher yields, central‑bank tightening and geopolitical shocks—is compressing fiscal space, elevating market volatility and reshaping monetary‑fiscal trade‑offs for advanced economies.
